extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (individuals or teams) in the Canadian social sciences and humanities preparing an application to SSHRC Insight Development Grants (February 2025 competition)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an application for the SSHRC Insight Development Grants (Feb 2025), meeting eligibility, budget, submission and merit-review requirements and addressing evaluation criteria (Challenge, Feasibility, Capability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge — The aim and importance of the endeavour (50%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the proposal’s relevance, originality and expected contribution to knowledge; appropriateness of literature review, theoretical approach, and methods; quality of training and mentoring; and potential for influence and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: 50%. For established scholars, reviewers consider: the proposal’s relevance to the objectives of the funding opportunity; originality, significance and expected contribution to knowledge; appropriateness of the literature review; appropriateness of the theoretical approach or framework; appropriateness of the methods/approach; quality of training and mentoring to be provided to students, emerging scholars and other highly qualified personnel, and opportunities for them to contribute; and potential for the project results to have influence and impact within and/or beyond the social sciences and humanities research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility — The plan to achieve excellence (20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project plan, timeline, team expertise, budget and knowledge mobilization make the objectives achievable within the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: 20%. Reviewers consider: appropriateness of the proposed timeline and probability that the objectives will be met; expertise of the applicant or team in relation to the proposed research; appropriateness of the requested budget, justification of proposed costs, and, where applicable, other financial and/or in‑kind contributions; and quality and appropriateness of knowledge mobilization plans, including for effective dissemination, exchange and engagement with stakeholders within and/or beyond the research community, where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability — The expertise to succeed (30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant(s)’s track record, past outputs and contributions to knowledge mobilization and research training relative to their roles and career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: 30%. Reviewers consider: quality, quantity and significance of past experience and published and/or creative outputs of the applicant and any co-applicants, relative to their roles in the project and the stage of their career; evidence of past knowledge mobilization activities (e.g., films, performances, commissioned reports, knowledge syntheses, experience in collaboration/other interactions with stakeholders, contributions to public debate and media), and of impacts on professional practice, social services and policies, etc.; and quality and quantity of past contributions to the development of effective research training and mentoring of students, postdoctoral researchers and other highly qualified personnel. Merit reviewers will consider information on only the last six years of research contributions; any career interruptions will be taken into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scheme and threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scoring ranges (1.00–6.00) with descriptors and requirement that applications must receive at least 'Moderate' for each criterion to be recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores: 1.00–1.83 = Excellent; 1.84–2.67 = Very good; 2.68–3.50 = Good; 3.51–4.33 = Satisfactory; 4.34–5.16 = Moderate; 5.17–6.00 = Unsatisfactory. The three criteria (Challenge, Feasibility, Capability) are weighted and combined; applications must receive a score in the 'Moderate' range (5.16–4.34) or better for each of the three criteria to be recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review process: single-stage committee review
rubrics_metrics.description: Insight Development Grant applications are evaluated via a single-stage committee review process that does not involve external assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions are based on merit review committee recommendations and available funds; committee discussions are guided by the principle of minimum essential funding. Merit review committees include national and international scholars and may include experts from other sectors. Normally, applications in the established stream initially ranked in the lowest 30% by committee consensus are not discussed during the final stage of merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee selection and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are asked to select the most appropriate review committee; SSHRC may determine the review process and committee assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants choose from discipline-based, groups of disciplines, multi/interdisciplinary (one humanities-focused and one social sciences-focused, plus Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee), or thematic committees. SSHRC will form committees based on application volume and reserves the right to determine an application’s review process and committee assignment. Applicants can contact SSHRC to discuss committee selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee (special process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications spanning mandates of more than one federal research funding agency may be submitted to a Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee which uses a harmonized tri-agency peer review process and specific evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to this committee must meet SSHRC’s Subject Matter Eligibility guidelines and the dominant component of the research must be in the social sciences and humanities. Tri-agency committee uses different criteria from the usual process used by this funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research (contextualization)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC’s Guidelines for the Merit Review of Indigenous Research are provided to reviewers to help interpret evaluation criteria in the context of Indigenous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines help build understanding of Indigenous research; SSHRC relies on reviewers with experience in Indigenous research. If enough Indigenous research applications are received, SSHRC may establish a distinct merit review committee. The guidelines are relevant both to applicants and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can involve any disciplines, thematic areas, approaches or subject areas eligible for SSHRC funding; certain project types are explicitly ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SSHRC’s guidelines on subject matter eligibility for details. Projects whose primary objective is curriculum development, preparation of teaching materials, program evaluation, organization of a conference or workshop, digitization of a collection or creation of a database are not eligible for funding under this funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget non‑eligible expense threshold (ineligibility rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be declared ineligible if 30% or more of the requested budget is allocated to non‑eligible expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requested budget avoids having ≥30% non‑eligible items; otherwise the application is ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant institutional affiliation and eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants (except postdoctoral fellows and PhD students) must be affiliated with a Canadian institution that holds institutional eligibility at time of application and before funding release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers whose primary affiliation is with a non‑Canadian postsecondary institution are not eligible for applicant status even if they maintain a Canadian affiliation. Applicants who previously received a SSHRC grant but failed to submit required achievement reports are not eligible to apply until reports are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral fellows and PhD candidate application conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs and eligible PhD candidates can be applicants but must establish a formal affiliation with an eligible Canadian postsecondary institution within three months of the grant start date and maintain it for the grant duration; PhD candidates must have met all PhD requirements before grant award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the current competition, affiliation must be established by September 2025. Eligible PhD students and postdoctoral fellows are encouraged to consult institutional Research Grants Offices early. Postdocs acting as applicants must meet institutional eligibility requirements for funds to be released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑applicant and collaborator eligibility and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Co‑applicants must be formally affiliated with eligible Canadian or international postsecondary institutions; collaborators are individuals who make a significant contribution and need not be affiliated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When international co-applicants are included, the application must clearly outline the rationale for international collaboration. Postdoctoral fellows and PhD candidates may be co-applicants under the same conditions as for applicants. Only a person named as co-applicant in the original application can replace an applicant (subject to program approval). Collaborators do not need an eligible Canadian affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications and holding multiple awards rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on submitting multiple applications and on holding concurrent awards between Insight Development Grants and other SSHRC programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals can apply as an applicant for only one Insight Development Grant at a time. Normally, researchers cannot apply as an applicant for an Insight Grant and an Insight Development Grant in the same calendar year, but SSHRC has an ongoing exception allowing unsuccessful Insight Development Grant applicants (Feb) to apply for an Insight Grant (Oct) of the same year. Researchers who applied for an Insight Grant in Oct 2024 can apply for an Insight Development Grant in Feb 2025 if research objectives are significantly different. See SSHRC regulations regarding multiple applications and holding multiple awards for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant holders must report on use of grant funds, funded activities and outcomes during the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants will be informed of reporting requirements in their Notice of Award. Grant holders are expected to report on the use of funds and on activities and outcomes undertaken during the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of Insight Development Grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific items that Insight Development Grant funds cannot be used for (and allowable exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insight Development Grant funds cannot be used for remuneration and/or travel and subsistence costs of presenters or guest speakers. Insight Development Grant funds cannot be used for collaborators’ research costs, although collaborators’ travel and subsistence expenses related to research planning/exchanging information or disseminating results are eligible. Consultation fees are eligible for expert/professional/technical services that contribute directly to the proposed research so long as the service is not being provided by a team member or other persons whose status would make them eligible to apply for a SSHRC grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of Tri‑Agency grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Tri-agency grant funds cannot be used to remunerate team members (applicant, co-applicant or collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes postdoctoral fellows serving in any of these capacities. Applicants must follow tri-agency financial rules where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Tri‑Agency policies and SSHRC regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants and grant holders must comply with SSHRC and Tri-Agency regulations and policies (financial administration, open access, research data management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must comply with Regulations Governing the Use of SSHRC Grant Funds, Tri-Agency Guide on Financial Administration, Tri-Agency Open Access Policy on Publications, and Tri‑Agency Research Data Management Policy (effective April 1, 2021). SSHRC reserves the right to determine eligibility and interpret regulations and policies governing funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern (STRAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications involving advancement of sensitive technology research areas will not be funded if researchers are affiliated with institutions connected to military, national defence or state security entities that could pose a risk to Canada's national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read tri-agency guidance on the STRAC policy to understand impacts. If the proposal falls within the federal government mandate and research is performed in government facilities, funding can only be allocated for student salaries, stipends and travel costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge mobilization expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated on the quality and appropriateness of knowledge mobilization plans and evidence of past knowledge mobilization activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge mobilization appears under Feasibility (plans) and Capability (evidence of past activities and impacts). Examples include films, performances, commissioned reports, knowledge syntheses, collaboration with stakeholders, contributions to public debate and media, and impacts on professional practice, social services and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and CV requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be completed using the application form and the Canadian Common CV (CCV) and submitted electronically by an authorized institutional officer (with exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants (and co-applicants) must complete the Canadian Common CV as part of the application process. Applications must be submitted electronically by an authorized research grants officer or equivalent from the applicant’s institution. Eligible PhD students and postdoctoral fellows can submit their applications directly to SSHRC. Applicants are encouraged to begin work on their CV early and consult the CCV FAQs and application instructions. Applicants needing help should contact SSHRC well in advance of the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition-specific funding distribution (emerging scholars reservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the current competition, at least 50% of funds will be reserved for applications from emerging scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a competition-specific allocation requirement and affects available funds and selection decisions for Feb 2025 competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and duration constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant values range and minimum budget requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insight Development Grants are valued at $7,000 to $75,000 over one to two years. A minimum budget of $7,000 is required in at least one of the years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible primary objectives (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project types explicitly not eligible as primary objectives for this funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects whose primary objective is curriculum development, preparation of teaching materials, program evaluation, organization of a conference or workshop, digitization of a collection or creation of a database are not eligible for funding under this funding opportunity.
